title: To Throw a Stone with Six Birds: On Agents and Agenthood
description:
To Throw a Stone with Six Birds: On Agents and Agenthood asks what it takes for a system to have choices that make a difference. It studies the question in finite controlled Markov kernels, without assuming goals, utilities, or an inner agent. Following Six Birds Theory (SBT), an agent is treated as a theory object: a package that is maintained inside an induced description of the system and that has a budgeted interface to the rest of the world. This separates agenthood, the existence and persistence of such a package, from agency, the ability of its interface choices to change what happens outside.

Three computable measures make the distinction concrete:

  • Viability kernel: the largest set of safe states in which every state has an affordable action whose possible successors all remain in the set.
  • Feasible empowerment: the channel capacity from affordable action sequences to a later outside variable.
  • Packaging defect: the idempotence defect of a coarse-grained packaging map.

Main results

  • Null tests: a single-action system has zero empowerment, and an external schedule mistaken for an action yields a spurious 1 bit.
  • With funded preventive repair, the packaging defect at a full phase cycle falls from 1 to 0 and the set of states that can be kept coherent grows from empty to 16; controls show that a zero defect alone does not identify maintenance.
  • A phase-dependent step (protocol holonomy) leaves one-step empowerment unchanged but raises the sampled median at two steps from 1.21 to 1.72 bits.
  • Reducing slip through a skill variable raises median empowerment from 0.84 to 1.37 bits.
  • With coherence required for safety, viability shows a change of support at zero noise and a repair-cost threshold set by the available income.
  • A Lean 4 development proves that the viability iteration reaches the greatest safe controlled-invariant set after at most as many strict removals as there are safe states.

All results are finite witnesses produced by deterministic, audited scripts. Code, experiment configurations, tests, and the Lean development are available at github.com/ioannist/six-birds-agent and archived at 10.5281/zenodo.18451887.
notes: Version 3 (6 October 2026). The capacity computation uses the standard Blahut-Arimoto update with explicit lower and upper stopping bounds, and all empowerment values were recomputed; the packaging experiment uses a funded substrate with controls; the order-dependence witness is reported with and without damage noise; the cost-only and combined cost-and-repair ablations are distinguished; the Lean development covers the viability operator itself with an iteration bound; the exposition, figures, and tables were revised throughout. See the version-history appendix of the paper.
